name: Residences at Delta II
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: TWG Development and the Delta Housing Authority are behind Residences at Delta II, a 50-unit family rental for households at 30% to 60% AMI next to the Residences at Delta I senior building on Villa Street in Delta. It won $1,449,981 a year in federal 9% credit and $700,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2024 Round One, and the financing closed in December 2024.
why_it_matters: It shows how a second phase in a small rural town can be built on the same site and with the same team as the first: the housing authority partnership supplies the property tax exemption and the management, and the city waived about $400,000 in fees.

background.text: Phase two of a campus: the family building sits next to Residences at Delta I, a 50-unit senior building TWG completed in 2023, and two Delta Housing Authority family tax credit properties, so the partners describe it as an intergenerational campus.

Local deal: the Delta Housing Authority is special limited partner, which brings a property tax exemption, and it manages the property. The City of Delta waived about $400,000 in tap, impact and permit fees.

Zoning: the application said the site was zoned for the use and only administrative plan review was needed. In August 2024 the Delta Planning Commission (2024-08-05) recommended and City Council (2024-08-20, first reading) approved a rezoning to allow the two-building, three-story development, requested by Residences at Delta, LLLP and TWG; the Delta Housing Authority supported it and a phase one senior resident raised noise and traffic concerns.

Need: the application cites a 3.8% submarket vacancy rate and a Delta Housing Authority waitlist of 428 applicants; the housing authority board chair cited 204 applicants at the August 2024 planning hearing.
Services: a part-time on-site service coordinator plus nonprofit programs (nutrition and wellness, education, intergenerational programs, veteran services, transportation).

Costs: the applicant says rural location drives costs up, with most materials trucked from Grand Junction about 40 miles away and a thin subcontractor pool. The Phase I environmental report found no recognized environmental conditions.

Financing team changed between application and closing: the application named Redstone Equity Partners as equity investor, while the December 2024 closing announcement lists Monarch Private Capital and Huntington Community Impact Capital among partners.
